title: Effects of interdisciplinary care on the course and health economic costs of Post-COVID syndrome
summary:
The aim of the study is to examine whether medical care involving multiple areas of expertise can provide better support for people experiencing ongoing health issues following a COVID-19 infection. Many affected individuals continue to suffer from symptoms such as severe fatigue, difficulty concentrating, or physical pain long after the initial illness. It is often unclear which treatments are truly effective, which can lead to unnecessary or unsuitable interventions.

As part of the study, 679 patients at the Post-COVID Center of the University Hospital Erlangen will be monitored over several months. They will take part in multiple surveys, reporting on their symptoms, quality of life, and experiences with medical care. In addition, discussion sessions with affected individuals and general practitioners will be held to better understand and improve the current healthcare approach.

The study aims to determine whether collaboration among different medical specialties improves the health and well-being of those affected, and whether it can also help reduce long-term healthcare costs. The findings are intended to support the targeted development of care for people with post-COVID conditions.

interventions.name: Intervention group (interdisciplinary care as part of comprehensive diagnostics at the Post-COVID Center Erlangen at T0)
Control group (patients on the center's waiting list, standard care by the general practitioner)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection that occurred at least three months ago, with post-COVID symptoms persisting for at least three months.
Exclusion criteria:
Post-vaccination syndrome,
Severe psychiatric and neurological disorders (e.g. psychosis, acute suicidality, dementia)
